findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD.

An employee was observed to change gloves without washing their hands and immediately moving to preparing a sandwich. Raw chicken was handled prior to this glove change. Education was conducted and the hands washed to correct. Ensure that hand washing takes place at all times required by the code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(B) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the dish machine would not produce a color change on the inspector’s test strips. Investigation revealed an empty container of sanitizer concentrate. The PIC was shown and had the jug replaced. A recheck later in the inspection still showed no color change on the chemical test strips. Education was conducted in relation to priming the machine. The machine was primed by the inspector and registered correctly afterwards.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16(A)(1) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY (TCS) FOOD shall be maintained: (1) At 57°C (135°F) or above.

Cheese sauce is observed in the far right well of the steam table and with an internal temperature of 128F. The cook was consulted and stated that the items came from the cooking process recently. This was supported by other observations made during the inspection. This container is the only item in this well and the other side is open. It is believed that this is the issue and that was stated to the cook. A lid was added to the back side to trap in the escaping heat. The cheese was allowed to be brought back up to temperature to save it and correct the violation. Ensure that all hot held TCS foods are maintained at 135F or hotter at all times in the facility.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

1) The inner wall of the cooler under the pizza prep station is observed soiled with food debris. 2) The chest freezer has major frost accumulation observed. Both locations were discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to clean and maintain clean moving forward. Ensure that all of the non-food contact surfaces are maintained clean to prevent possible contamination in the kitchen.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

1) The floor in the walk in cooler is in need of cleaning, especially under the shelves, along the walls and in the corners. 2) The wall next to the fryer is observed heavily soiled with baked on grease. These two locations were discussed with the PIC and they are instructed to clean prior to the next routine inspection. Ensure that all facilities are maintained clean at all times.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.citation_text:
6-403.11(B) Designated Areas. (B) Lockers or other suitable facilities shall be located in a designated room or area where contamination of FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLESERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES can not occur.

A personal water bottle is observed in the standing cooler next to the manager’s office intermixed with foods intended for consumers. The PIC was told and instructed to remove. Ensure that all employee foods are stored separately from foods intended for consumers at all times. The bottle was removed to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11(C) Equipment Food-Contact Surfaces and Utensils. (C) Except as specified in (D) of this section, if used with TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD, EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be cleaned throughout the day at least every 4 hours.

Multiple dishes in the storage area were observed with remaining food debris, oil or a sticky substance still on them. Several of these items are still wet from recent washing. The PIC was shown and moved the items back to dish for recleaning to correct. Ensure that dishes are being completely cleaned prior to storage.

findings.title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding.
findings.citation_text:
3-403.11(A) Reheating for Hot Holding. (A) Except as specified under (B) and (C) and in (E) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD that is cooked, cooled, and reheated for hot holding shall be reheated so that all parts of the FOOD reach a temperature of at least 74°C (165°F) for 15 seconds. 

A pan of cheese sauce on the prep line was observed at 114F internal temperature during this inspection. Investigation showed that it was pulled from its reheating process to early due to a miscommunication in the kitchen. The cheese was on the cook line approximately 30-45 minutes prior to observation per the cook that pulled it. The pan was allowed to be brought to the stove for rapid reheating to be saved. Another pan was above 165F and moved to the steam table for service to correct. Ensure that the reheating process is completed each time in the facility.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored.
findings.citation_text:
3-304.12(C) In-Use Utensils, Between-Use Storage. During pauses in FOOD preparation or dispensing, FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored:(C) On a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food-contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized at a frequency specified under §§ 4-602.11 and 4-702.11.

1) The probe thermometers on the cook line are observed in a cup that is spoiled with food debris and oil accumulation. 2) The knife used at the sandwich perp cooler was observed in the open space between the two cooler lids. This space was cleanable but was not observed clean at the time of the inspection. Both locations were shown to the PIC and the food contact items removed for cleaning. The storage surfaces were also cleaned and sanitized to correct the violation. Ensure that all food contact items are stored so that they are protected from contamination at all times.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.citation_text:
5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

Three sinks in the facility were observed with leaks at the faucet. The sinks were the bar three part sink, the sprayer faucet by the dish machine and the faucet at the mop sink. The PIC was instructed to have the sinks repaired to remove the leaked prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.citation_text:
3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

Several cans in the dry storage room are observed with major dents. The PIC was shown and removed the items for credit during this inspection to correct. Ensure that the package integrity is maintained at all times for the stored foods in the facility.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display.

1) Raw fish is observed over raw beef in the standing cooler to the left of the fryers. 2) Raw sausage is observed over Ready-To-Eat (RTE) deli meats in the walk in cooler. The PIC was shown both locations and adjusted the storage to correct. Ensure that items in a cooler are stored with the RTE items on top, then raw vegetables, raw sea food, raw beef/pork and raw chicken on the bottom to prevent contamination based on the relative cooking temperatures of the items.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11(A) Equipment, Utensils, Linens, and Single-Service and Single-Use Articles. (A) Except as specified in (D) of this section, cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

The container used for storing Dixie cups along the prep and service lines is observed soiled. The PIC was shown and had the container washed and items replaced to correct. Ensure that single service items are protected from contamination until use.

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

All of the Allergen training certificates available at the facility have expired at the end of last year. The PIC was notified and instructed to have the current CFPMs retake the course/renew the certification. Ensure that all CFPMs at the facility maintain current allergen training certifications at all times.

findings.comment:

Multiple shelves in the walk in cooler and walk in freezer have had their smooth coating worn away and are beginning to rust. The PIC was shown and instructed to repair/replace so that a smooth and easily cleanable surface is maintained at all times.

findings.comment:
4-602.11: (A) FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be cleaned before each use, each time there is a change in work, between uses of raw FOODS to RTE FOODS, before using FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE, and when contamination has occurred. (C) Cleaned at least every 4 hours. 

1) A knife stored as ready for use on the magnetic rack in the back hallway has dried on food debris. 2) Pans in the dry storage room are observed with dry food debris on them. Both items were shown to the PIC and moved to dish for re-cleaning. Ensure that all food contact items are cleaned completely prior to storage.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The inner door of the right ice machine has multiple black spots observed on it. These locations appear to have moisture flowing through the locations as well. The PIC was shown and the lid cleaned during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C] 

1) A small mold colony appears to be developing above the door to the walk in freezer. 2) Multiple racks in the walk in cooler need significant cleaning along the tray storage shelves. 3) Wire shelves in the walk in cooler are in need of cleaning. These situations were shown to the PIC and they are instructed to clean and maintain them clean moving forward. Maintain clean facilities.

Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris. 

The counter leading into the dish machine appears to be falling from the wall exposing a gap between it and the sheet metal above. Re-seal the gap prior to the next routine inspection. Repairing the counter so that it lines up correctly is suggested to make this easier.

2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

1) Quat sanitizer in the bar area bucket is observed at approximately 50 ppm concentration. 2) (REPEAT) Quat sanitizer along the kitchen cook line is observed to not register on the inspector’s test strips. Both buckets were remade during this inspection to correct the violation, but this is the second time that the cook line has not been at effective/acceptable concentration.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

An ice bath is observed with containers of both shredded cheese and cooked pasta shells sitting on top of the ice. Per employee/PIC the items are brought out of the cooler for lunch and dinner rushes then returned to coolers after. Cold holding and ice baths were discussed and the items noted discarded to correct the immediately violation. A suggestion for keeping foods in proper cold holding requirements included ensuring that the ice is higher than the level of the foods, but only if foods can be maintained in temperature. Otherwise the items will need to be discarded after every rush to ensure safety.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). 

A mostly used gallon of milk is observed in one of the standing server coolers. Employee indicated that it had been opened Monday (3/13/23). Inspector discussed 7 day date marking and a date was added to the container to correct.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. 

Fish are observed in standing water in the three part sink at the rear of the kitchen. Thawing in this situation should be conducted with running water. Water was turned back on to correct the violation.

Violation awarded today and the PICs are instructed to maintain the floors clean and cleanable.

Drink/foods intended for employees should be stored so that they do not pose a risk of contaminating foods intended for consumers.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Numerous employee’s food handler cards have expired by the time of this inspection. Discussed with PIC and instructed them to ensure that food handler cards are renewed prior to expiration. Follow up on the next routine inspection.

findings.title: No bare hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed
findings.comment:
Employee observed handling an edible taco shell bowl with bare hands. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC, who had employee discard the bowl, wash hands, and don gloves. Do not handle ready-to-eat food with bare hands.

3-801.11: (D) FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact READY-TO-EAT FOOD as specified under  3-301.11(B) and (E). [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
No measurable quat sanitizer observed in the cookline sanitizer bucket. Upon investigation, no sanitizer was connected to the wall-mounted dispenser. CORRECTED- PIC remade bucket to a concentration of 400ppm quat. Sanitizer was reattached to wall-mounted dispenser.

4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have a concentration based on label (200-400ppm), and water with 500ppm hardness or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
2nd REPEAT: The following hot-held foods observed out of temperature (probed): grilled chicken at 126F, and chili at 127F. CORRECTED- Food were rapidly reheated to 165F. Hot holding equipment was adjusted to ensure foods maintain temperature of 135F or above.

3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. [P]

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
Two 5-inch-deep half pans of cheese sauce observed cooling in the walk-in cooler, tightly covered with plastic wrap. Both containers observed to be 135F, probed. Pans were moved to hot holding for service today. Any remaining at the end of service will be moved to shallow pans to cool and will be reheated again tomorrow. Ensure techniques are used to help cooling foods reach 41F quickly, including shallow pans, ice baths, and leaving pans uncovered if otherwise protected from contamination.

3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. [C]

Observed the area under the ice container and soda gun at the bar to be soiled with dirt, food, and other debris. Ensure this area is cleaned routinely so it is maintained clean. Additionally, areas under and behind booths should be cleaned frequently, This will be checked during the follow-up scheduled for 8-22-22. 

6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
Two uncovered employee beverages observed in the kitchen: a Starbucks drink on the finishing line and a lemon drink on the back prep counter. CORRECTED- Employee beverages discarded. Discussed with PIC to educate staff on beverages- must be covered with a lid and a straw.
2-401.11: (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS. [C]

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: The following hot-held foods observed out of temperature (probed): meat sauce at 100F, and ground beef at 104F. CORRECTED- Food were rapidly reheated to 165F and flames were relit on the hot holding unit to ensure temperature is maintained.
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. [P]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Foods in both prep coolers observed out of temperature. In the long prep cooler, the following were observed: diced tomato at 51F, shredded cheese at 46F, shredded mozzarella at 48F, pepperoni at 43F, pizza sauce at 45F, sausage at 44F, and feta cheese at 45F. Foods in the lower portion of the cooler were observed 41F or below. Low pans are typically discarded at 4PM (shift change). Out of temperature foods were voluntarily discarded or moved to the walk-in cooler to rapidly chill to 41F or below since foods were in temperature at open at 11AM.

In the shorter prep cooler, the following were observed out of temperature: sliced tomato at 59F, shredded cheese at 59F, sauerkraut at 59F, provolone cheese at 57F, sliced cheese at 58F, sliced tomato at 53F, and deli meats at 53F. Foods above 55F were voluntarily discarded. Foods 55F or below were moved to the walk-in cooler to rapidly cool since they were in temperature at open at 11AM. PIC adjusted cooler settings.

Inspector will follow up to see that coolers are functioning properly. Discussed monitoring coolers and the use of time as a control in the meantime.

3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
A container of taco meat was observed in the walk-in cooler dated 6/25. CORRECTED- Discussed with PIC. Out of date taco meat voluntarily discarded.
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. [P]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
Boxes observed stored on the floor in the dry storage area and in the walk-in freezer. Ensure that foods are stored at least 6 inches off the ground to prevent contamination from the facility and to allow cleaning around/under items.
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. (B) FOOD in working containers and packages may be stored less than 6 inches on case lot handling EQUIPMENT. (C) Pressurized BEVERAGE containers, cased FOOD in waterproof containers, and milk containers in plastic crates may be stored on floor. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: Broken floor tiles (one almost completely missing) observed in the walk-in around the door between cooler and freezer. Repair floor tiles.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Coving is missing around the dish area. Replace coving so that floor and wall are sealed together and any gap is eliminated.
6-201.13: (A) floor and wall junctures shall be coved and closed to no larger than 1mm (one thirty-second inch). (B) Floors in which water flush cleaning methods are used shall be provided with drains and be graded to drain. Floor and wall junctures shall be coved and SEALED. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Soil accumulation observed under shelving in the walk-in cooler, under the handsink/soda gun area of the bar, and under counters in the kitchen. Clean as often as necessary to prevent soil accumulation.
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
Bar handwashing sink observed containing a strainer and metal pan. CORRECTED— Items removed from bar handsink. Ensure sink is always clear and accessible to allow frequent handwashing.
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. [Pf]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Raw salmon observed stored above a head of lettuce. CORRECTED— Salmon moved to lower shelf. Lettuce removed from cooler. Ensure foods are stored to prevent potential for cross contamination.
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. [P]

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
The following hot-held foods observed out of temperature (probed): meat sauce at 110F; green beans at 115F; and mashed potatoes at 110F. CORRECTED— Foods prepared about 2 hours ago, so they were rapidly reheated to 165F for service. Maintain hot held foods at 135F or above.
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. [P]

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.comment:
Floor drain near the ice machine is clogged, causing wastewater pooling in that area. CORRECTED— Staff snaked the drain. Wastewater is draining. Ensure wastewater handled properly through approved disposal systems.
5-403.11: SEWAGE shall be disposed through an APPROVED facility that is: (A) A public SEWAGE treatment plant (B) An individual SEWAGE disposal system that is sized, constructed, maintained, and operated according to LAW. [P]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Broken floor tiles (one almost completely missing) observed in the walk-in around the door between cooler and freezer. Repair floor tiles.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
1st REPEAT: None of the CFMs present have completed ANSI approved allergen awareness training. Complete allergen training.
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
Foods in the top of prep cooler #3 (farthest from the office) observed as follows: sliced roast beef at 44F; diced tomatoes at 50F; and sliced tomatoes at 50F. In the bottom of the prep cooler, sliced tomatoes observed at 43F and sauerkraut at 46F. CORRECTED— Items from the bottom of the cooler were relocated to the walk-in cooler. Foods in the top of the prep cooler were put on ice to maintain temperature at 41F or below.
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. [P]

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
— Food in the walk-in cooler (meat sauce, pizza sauce, and chili/ground beef) observed stored without covers on middle shelves. Cover food to prevent potential contamination from above. CORRECTED— Foods covered.
— Ice bin left open while bar was unattended. Ensure foods (including ice) are protected from potential contamination. CORRECTED— Covered.
— Open package of fries observed on the floor on the prep line. CORRECTED— Fries moved to walk-in freezer to be stored up off the ground.
3-305.11: (A) FOOD shall be protected from contamination: In clean dry location, not exposed to any form of contamination, at least 6 inches above floor. [C]

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
Prep cooler #1 (closest to the office) observed to have a gash in the interior of the door that causes it to no longer be smooth or easily cleanable. Repair/patch damaged door.
4-202.16: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES shall be free of unnecessary ledges, projections, and crevices, and designed and constructed to allow easy cleaning and to facilitate maintenance. [C]

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
None of the CFMs present have completed ANSI approved allergen awareness training. Complete allergen training.
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. [C]

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment: Container of red sauce observed uncovered on a middle shelf of the walk in cooler with other foods stored above. CORRECTED-- Covered food to protect from cross contamination during storage.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11 (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display. (P)

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Can opener observed with an accumulation of build-up on the blade. Clean after each use and as often as necessary to maintain clean. CORRECTED-- Can opener removed to be washed, rinsed, and sanitized.
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. (Pf)

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Multiple foods (cooked beef, red sauce, sliced deli meats) observed in the walk-in cooler without date-markings. CORRECTED-- PIC labeled foods with the dates they were prepared.
3-501.17: (A) Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1. (Pf)
